skill.title: Classify a function as injective, surjective, bijective

candidates.question:
The function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x) = 5 - \frac{2x}{3}$.
Decide whether $f$ is injective, surjective and bijective, giving a reason for each.

lines.text: $f$ is injective if $f(a) = f(b)$ forces $a = b$.
Equal outputs force equal inputs, so $f$ is injective.
$f$ is surjective if every $y$ in the codomain $\mathbb{R}$ equals $f(x)$ for some $x$ in the domain.
This $x$ is a real number for every real $y$, so every $y$ is reached and $f$ is surjective.
$f$ is both injective and surjective, so it is bijective.

candidates.final: f \text{ is injective, surjective and bijective}

candidates.question:
The function $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $g(x) = x^2 - 6x + 5$.
Decide whether $g$ is injective, surjective and bijective, giving a reason for each.

steps.title: Test injectivity: look for two inputs with the same output

lines.text: Two different inputs, $0$ and $6$, give the same output, so $g$ is not injective.

steps.title: Test surjectivity: find the smallest output

lines.text: Since $(x - 3)^2 \ge 0$, every output satisfies $g(x) \ge -4$. Test a value below $-4$, such as $-5$.
A square cannot be negative, so there is no real $x$ with $g(x) = -5$. Then $-5$ is in the codomain but is never reached, so $g$ is not surjective.
$g$ is neither injective nor surjective, so it is not bijective.

candidates.final: g \text{ is neither injective nor surjective, so not bijective}

candidates.question:
The function $h : \{1, 2, 3\} \to \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ is defined by $h(x) = x + 1$.
Decide whether $h$ is injective, surjective and bijective, giving a reason for each.

lines.text: The outputs $2, 3, 4$ are all different, so different inputs give different outputs and $h$ is injective.
The codomain is $\{1, 2, 3, 4\}$. The element $1$ is not an output, because $x + 1 = 1$ gives $x = 0$, which is not in the domain. So $h$ is not surjective.
$h$ is injective but not surjective, so it is not bijective. (A bijection needs the same number of elements in the domain and codomain: here $3 \ne 4$.)

candidates.final: h \text{ is injective, not surjective, so not bijective}

skill.title: Compare data sets with back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots

candidates.question:

Boys: $21, 34, 27, 25, 32, 38, 29, 24, 35, 31, 27, 40, 33, 26$
Girls: $28, 35, 42, 31, 39, 45, 33, 37, 41, 36, 44, 30, 38, 49$
Draw a back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot of the data, using the tens digits as stems. Use the median and the range to compare the two sets.

lines.text: The stems go down the middle. Boys leaves go on the left and Girls leaves on the right, smallest next to the stem.
Key: $2 | 5 = 25$ hundredths of a second.
There are 14 values, so the median is the mean of the 7th and 8th.

skill.title: Test whether a point is on a line; find intercepts

candidates.question:
The line $k$ has equation $3x - 2y - 12 = 0$.
Find the points where $k$ cuts the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, and test whether the point $(6, 3)$ is on $k$.

lines.text: The line cuts the $x$-axis at $(4, 0)$.
The line cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, -6)$.
The left side equals $0$, so $(6, 3)$ is on $k$.

candidates.question:
The line $l$ has equation $y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 4$.
Find the points where $l$ cuts the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, and test whether the point $(3, 3)$ is on $l$.

lines.text: The line cuts the $x$-axis at $(6, 0)$.
The line cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, 4)$.

steps.title: Substitute x = 3 into the right side

lines.text: The line gives $y = 2$ when $x = 3$, but the point has $y = 3$. Since $2 \ne 3$, $(3, 3)$ is not on $l$.

candidates.question:
The line $m$ has equation $2x - 5y = 10$.
Find the points where $m$ cuts the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis, and test whether the point $(10, 2)$ is on $m$.

lines.text: The line cuts the $x$-axis at $(5, 0)$.
The line cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, -2)$.
The left side equals $10$, which is the right side, so $(10, 2)$ is on $m$.
